content.text: : antimalarial drug; inhibits release of IL-1; other actions include inhibition of T cells, B cells, and antigen processing in monocytes and macrophages
: ingested by macrophages; suppress phagocytosis and lysosomal enzyme release and activity; ↓ RF and IgG’s
: mild RA for pts w/ inadequate response to NSAIDs
: blood dyscrasias (aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia), proteinuria, hematuria

: immunomodulatory agent that suppresses proinflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL1); exerts some anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting chemotaxis and neutrophil migration, decreasing angiogenesis, and enhancing adenosine release
Metabolized to sulfapyridine (sulfonamide antimicrobial) and a salicylate (5-aminosalicylic acid)
: GI disturbances (MC), SJS/TEN, blood dyscrasias (agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), hemolytic anemia

: antimetabolite; interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR); MOA in RA is unknown, but is thought to be similar to the antineoplastic action: folate antagonist that inhibits synthesis of purines
: usually first choice of DMARD therapy
: pregnancy/lactating, alcoholism, hepatic disease, immunodeficiency syndromes, preexisting blood dyscrasias
: GI (N/V/D, stomatitis) alopecia, elevated serum transaminases, skin (rash, pruritis, urticaria), CNS (fatigue, HA, malaise)
•less common – bone marrow suppression, immunosuppression, interstitial pneumonitis, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis
: derivative of 6-mercaptopurine and acts as an immunosuppressive antimetabolite
: approved for severe RA; restrict use to pts w/ severe, active & erosive disease not responsive to conventional management
: active metabolite malononitrilamide – immunomodulatory agent that inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase; antiproliferative & anti-inflammatory effects
: first oral agent for active RA labeled for slowing disease progression; relieves arthritis symptoms and halts structural damage to joints
: pregnancy/lactation, administration of live vaccines, immunocompromised pts not recommended
: elevated serum transaminases, GI (N/D, abdominal pain), rash, reversible alopecia, SJS/TEN, myelosuppression (pancytopenia, agranulocytosis)
: inhibition of JAK1 and JAK3 blocks the signaling of several cytokines such as interleukins 2,4,7,9,15, and 21; this blockade is thought to modulate the immune response and inflammation in RA
•adults w/ moderately to severely active RA who have has an inadequate response or intolerance to MTX
•monotherapy or in combination w/ MTX or other nonbiologic DMARDs
•should not be used in combination w/ biologic DMARDs or potent immunosuppressants, such as azathioprine or cyclosporine
: decreased LDL, HA, UTIs, nasopharyngitis, URI, increased risk of blood clots, PE, thrombosis, VTE, skin cancer, GI perforation
: binds to TNF, competitively inhibiting the binding of TNF to target cell surface receptors
•considered an appropriate option for pts who respond sub-optimally to any DMARD, particularly MTX
•moderate to severe active RA (w/ or w/o MTX)
•Juvenile RA (pts 4-17yo), psoriatic arthritis, severe plaque psoriasis
: injection site reactions, development of autoantibodies, serious infections (TB, bacterial, fungal), depress immune response, may increase incidence of infections/mortality in sepsis
: demyelinating disorders in CNS, pancytopenia (aplastic anemia), increased incidence of lymphoma in children/adolescents
: binds to TNF, competitively inhibiting the binding of TNF to target cell surface receptors
•moderate to severe RA in combination w/ MTX
: infusion reactions (dyspnea, flushing, HA, rash), infections (URI, UTI)

: hepatotoxicity, infections (sepsis, pneumonia), TB infection, hematological (leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia), neuro events (optic neuritis, seizures, CNS demyelinating disorders), immunogenicity, hypersensitivity (urticaria, dyspnea, hypotension, serum sickness)
: human recombinant IgG1 monoclonal antibody which blocks actions of TNF at p55 and p75 surface TNFR on target cells
: moderately to severely active RA who have had insufficient response to one or more DMARDs; can be used alone or in combination w/ MTX or other DMARDs
: injection site reactions, infections (URI, UTI, TB, bronchitis), exacerbation of demyelinating diseases, malignancies
: moderately to severely active RA in adults, in combination w/ MTX; active psoriatic arthritis & ankylosing spondylitis
: increased risk of serious infection (TB, sepsis, invasive fungal), HBV reactivation
: use in pts w/ hx of hf or CNS demyelinating disorders
: contains a PEGylated humanized Fab’ region; lacks an Fc region; minimizes Fc-mediated effects
: treatment of moderate-severe RA as monotherapy or in combination w/ DMARDs
: IL1 receptor antagonist; blockade of IL1 signals results in decreased inflammation, pannus formation, & bone resorption
•reduction in s/sxs & slowing progression of structural damage of moderately-severely active RA in adults ≥18yo who have failed therapy w/ ≥1 DMARD
•used alone or in combination w/ DMARDs
•combination w/ MTX effective when inadequate response to MTX alone
•not used concurrently w/ TNF neutralizing agents
•do not initiate in pts w/ active infections & D/C if serious infection develops
: serious infections (higher incidence w/ concurrent asthma)
: recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody that blocks IL6 receptor
•treatment of adult pts w/ moderately-severely active RA who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF blockers

•used alone or given in combination w/ MTX or other DMARDs, but not w/ other biologics – when given w/ MTX → inhibition & slowing of structural joint damage, improvement of physical function, & achievement of major clinical response in adults w/ moderately-severely active RA
: do not give to pts w/ an active infection; test for latent TB before starting therapy
: increased risk of serious infections (bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, TB)

: costimulation modulator which inhibits T cell activation; decreases T-cell proliferation, inhibits cytokine production and release from activated macrophages and fibroblasts → decreases levels of TNF, gamma interferon (IFNgamma), and IL2, decreases B cell activation and autoantibody production (lower titers of RF)
: monotherapy or in combination w/ MTX or another nonbiologic DMARD in adults w/ moderate-severe RA who have had an incomplete response to oral DMARDs or TNF antagonists
: serious infections (pneumonia, cellulitis, UTI, bronchitis), malignancies, acute infusion reactions, hypersensitivity
•concurrent therapy w/ TNF antagonists is not recommended due to increased incidences of infections
•D/C if a serious infection develops – screen for TB
•do not give live vaccines concurrently or within 3mo of D/C

: chimeric murine/human recombinant monoclonal antibody directed against the CD20 antigen found on the surface of normal and malignant B cells; the Fab portion binds specifically to the CD20 on pre-B and mature B cells and the Fc portion assists in mediating B-cell lysis
: indicated in combination w/ MTX to reduce s/sxs in adult pts w/ moderately-severely active RA who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonists
: fatal infusion reactions, tumor lysis syndrome, severe mucocutaneous reactions
: positive PPD does not require tx before starting Rituximab, screen for HBV before starting
